scenes.body: A recipe card for chai takes **inputs** (water, milk, sugar), does the **same steps** every time, and **gives back** one thing: a cup of chai. Write the card once, use it every morning.

scenes.title: A class is a cookie cutter
scenes.body: One **cookie cutter** (the class) makes many **cookies** (objects). Every cookie has the same shape, but each can have its own toppings (its **attributes**). What a cookie can do is its **methods**.

scenes.title: Exceptions are a fire alarm
scenes.body: When something goes wrong, an **alarm rings** (an exception is raised). If **someone responds** (`except`), the building keeps working. If nobody does, everything **stops**. A good building has alarms for specific problems, not one for everything.

scenes.heading: Exceptions: try, except, else, finally
scenes.title: exceptions.py

steps.note: `try`: code that might fail.
`except ValueError`: runs **only** for that error type.
`else`: runs only if **no** exception happened.
`finally`: **always** runs, success or failure. Perfect for cleanup.

items.q: What is `self` in a Python method?
items.a: The object the method was called on. `chat.add(...)` runs `Conversation.add(chat, ...)`, so `self` is `chat`. It lets each object keep its **own** data.
items.trap: Thinking `self` is a keyword. It's just the conventional name of the first parameter.

items.a: The default list is created **once** and shared by every call that uses it, so data leaks between calls. Use `items=None` and create a new list inside (or `field(default_factory=list)` in a dataclass).
items.trap: Fixing it with `items=list()`. That's still evaluated once.

items.q: When should you write a bare `except:`?
items.a: Almost never. Catch the **specific** exceptions you can handle. If you must catch broadly (for example at the top of a server), catch `Exception`, **log** it, and don't hide it.
items.trap: `except: pass`: it also swallows `KeyboardInterrupt` and your own bugs.

scenes.question: Why is `def add(msg, history=[])` dangerous?
options: The same list is shared by every call that uses the default
scenes.explain: Default values are created **once**, when the function is defined. Use `history=None` and create a new list inside.

scenes.question: In `try / except / else / finally`, which block runs **every** time?
scenes.explain: `finally` runs whether the `try` succeeded or failed. `else` runs only on success; `except` only on a matching error.
